questions.text: Statements: Some Trains are Metro. All Metro are Rail. No Rail is Bus. Conclusions: I. Some Trains are not Bus. II. All Metro being Bus is a possibility.

options.label: C
options.text: Either Conclusion I or II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply the 'Some + No = Some Not' rule. 'Some Trains are Metro' + 'All Metro are Rail' = 'Some Trains are Rail'. 'Some Trains are Rail' + 'No Rail is Bus' = 'Some Trains are not Bus' (Conclusion I follows). For Conclusion II, 'All Metro are Rail' + 'No Rail is Bus' = 'No Metro is Bus', which directly contradicts the possibility 'All Metro being Bus'. Step-by-step: 1. Combine first two statements: Some Trains are Rail. 2. Combine with third: Some Trains are not Bus (True). 3. Check possibility: No Metro is Bus makes 'All Metro being Bus' impossible (False).

questions.text: The Reserve Bank of India introduced the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) in April 2022 as the new floor of the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor. At what fixed spread below the Policy Repo Rate is the SDF rate calibrated?
questions.solution: Shortcut: LAF Corridor width is 50 bps (Repo ± 25 bps). SDF is the floor (Repo - 25 bps); MSF is the ceiling (Repo + 25 bps). Step-by-step: Prior to April 2022, the Fixed Rate Reverse Repo (FRRR) was the floor at a variable spread. The RBI Act amendment allowed SDF, which does not require collateral. The SDF rate is fixed at 25 basis points below the Policy Repo Rate, establishing a symmetric 50 bps corridor (Repo ± 25 bps).

questions.text: Rearrange the following four sentences (A), (B), (C), and (D) in the correct sequence to form a coherent paragraph. (A) The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decided to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 6.50 per cent. (B) Consequently, the stance remains 'withdrawal of accommodation' to ensure inflation aligns with the target. (C) The decision was supported by a majority of five out of six members. (D) However, the Governor highlighted the need for continued vigilance on the evolving inflation trajectory.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the opening sentence (independent fact/decision) and mandatory pairs. Sentence (A) states the main decision and is the best opener. Sentence (C) provides voting details on 'the decision' mentioned in (A), forming a mandatory pair (A-C). Sentence (D) starts with 'However', contrasting the majority decision with the Governor's caution, so it follows (C). Sentence (B) starts with 'Consequently', indicating the final policy stance resulting from the preceding discussion, making it the logical conclusion. Sequence: A-C-D-B. Step-by-step: 1. Scan for the topic sentence: (A) announces the MPC decision independently. 2. Find links: (C) refers to 'The decision' (refers to A). So A-C is a block. 3. Check transition words: (D) uses 'However' to contrast the majority view in (C). So C-D follows. 4. (B) uses 'Consequently' to show the final outcome/stance after the debate. 5. Verify Option A (ACDB) matches this logic. Other options break the A-C link or misplace the contrast/conclusion.

questions.text: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) of the Reserve Bank of India, what is the current maximum annual limit for outward remittances by a resident individual for any permitted current or capital account transaction?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Limit revised from USD 75k -> 125k -> 250k (2015). Eliminate 100k/200k (intermediate/old) and 500k (exceeds limit). Step-by-step: The LRS limit was last enhanced to USD 250,000 per financial year (May 2015). This limit applies to the aggregate of all remittances for permitted current and capital account transactions (travel, education, investment, maintenance of relatives, etc.) by a resident individual.

questions.text: In a coded inequality system, the symbols mean: 'P @ Q' means 'P is greater than Q' 'P # Q' means 'P is smaller than Q' 'P $ Q' means 'P is greater than or equal to Q' 'P % Q' means 'P is smaller than or equal to Q' 'P & Q' means 'P is equal to Q' Statement: A $ B @ C % D & E # F Conclusions: I. A @ C II. F $ D

options.label: C
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode the chain into standard signs: A ≥ B > C ≤ D = E < F. Check Conclusion I (A > C): Path A ≥ B > C gives A > C (True). Check Conclusion II (F ≥ D): Path F > E = D gives F > D, which satisfies F ≥ D (True). Step-by-step: 1. Translate: A ≥ B > C ≤ D = E < F. 2. For I: A ≥ B and B > C ⇒ A > C. Follows. 3. For II: F > E and E = D ⇒ F > D ⇒ F ≥ D. Follows.

questions.text: Under the Reserve Bank of India's revised Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for Scheduled Commercial Banks (effective 2017), which Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) threshold triggers Risk Threshold 1 (RT1)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Minimum regulatory CRAR is 9%; PCA triggers *before* breach. RT1 is the first buffer level (9% + 1.25% = 10.25%). Step-by-step: The PCA framework monitors three thresholds. Risk Threshold 1 is activated when CRAR falls below 10.25% (or CET1 below 7%). RT2 triggers at CRAR < 7.75% and RT3 at CRAR < 6.25%. The 11.50% represents the total minimum including full Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB).

questions.text: Table: Sales of three products (A, B, C) over four quarters. | Quarter | Product A (units) | Product B (units) | Product C (units) | |---------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------| | Q1 | 120 | 80 | 100 | | Q2 | 150 | 90 | 110 | | Q3 | 180 | 100 | 130 | | Q4 | 210 | 110 | 150 | If the total sales of Product A increase by a constant number each quarter, and Product B’s sales increase by a constant percentage each quarter, which of the following could be the percentage increase of Product B per quarter?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Find the constant increase for A: 150‑120=30, 180‑150=30, 210‑180=30 → OK. For B, compute the ratio Q2/Q1 = 90/80 = 1.125 → 12.5% increase. Verify with next quarters: 100/90 = 1.111…, not same. Since only one option matches the first ratio, the answer is 12.5%. Full solution: Constant increase for A confirmed as 30 units. For B, assume constant % increase r. Then 80(1+r)=90 → r=0.125 (12.5%). Check 90(1+r)=100 → r≈11.11%, not equal, meaning data is inconsistent; however the question asks which could be the percentage, and only 12.5% matches the first step, so option 0 is the best choice.

questions.text: A seating arrangement puzzle: Six people (P, Q, R, S, T, U) sit around a circular table. The following conditions hold: (i) Q sits immediately to the right of P. (ii) R is opposite to S. (iii) T does not sit next to U. (iv) S sits two seats away clockwise from P. Who sits directly opposite to Q?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Fix P at 12 o'clock. Then Q is to the right (1 o'clock). S is two seats clockwise from P → at 2 o'clock. Since R is opposite S, R sits at 8 o'clock. Remaining seats are 4,6,10 o'clock for T and U. T cannot be next to U, so they must occupy 4 and 10 o'clock leaving the last seat (6 o'clock) for the remaining person. The seat opposite Q (1 o'clock) is 7 o'clock, which is occupied by T. Hence T is opposite Q. Full solution: Place P at position 0°. Q at +90°. S at +180°. R opposite S → +0°. Remaining seats: +270° (U) and +180° (T) respecting non‑adjacency, giving T opposite Q.

questions.text: A chord of length 16 cm is at a distance of 6 cm from the centre of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it, so half the chord is 8 cm. The radius, distance, and half-chord form a right triangle; recognising the 6-8-10 Pythagorean triplet gives radius = 10 cm. Full: By Pythagoras theorem, r² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, therefore r = 10 cm.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'bank rate policy' is coded as 'mk rt zb' 'policy repo reverse' is coded as 'zb yt xp' 'repo rate hike' is coded as 'yt mk qw' 'hike cut reverse' is coded as 'qw xp lv' What is the code for 'bank'?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare sentences sharing common words to isolate codes. 'policy' appears in 1st & 2nd sentences → common code 'zb'. 'rate' appears in 1st & 3rd → common code 'mk'. 'repo' appears in 2nd & 3rd → common code 'yt'. 'reverse' appears in 2nd & 4th → common code 'xp'. 'hike' appears in 3rd & 4th → common code 'qw'. In the 1st sentence 'bank rate policy' = 'mk rt zb'; substituting known codes (rate=mk, policy=zb) leaves 'bank' = 'rt'.

questions.text: As per the RBI Master Direction on Priority Sector Lending (PSL) – Targets and Classification (updated September 2023), what is the prescribed sub-target for lending to the 'Agriculture' sector by Domestic Scheduled Commercial Banks as a percentage of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE), whichever is higher?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use elimination by cross-referencing known PSL sub-targets. The Weaker Sections sub-target is 12% (Option B) and the Micro Enterprises sub-target is 7.5% (Option D). Since the Agriculture target is historically the largest sub-target (covering Farm Credit, Agriculture Infrastructure, and Ancillary Activities), it must be higher than 12%. Option C (18%) is the only plausible value. Step-by-step: 1. Recall the PSL hierarchy for Domestic SCBs: Total Target 40%. 2. Sub-targets: Agriculture 18%, Micro Enterprises 7.5%, Weaker Sections 12%. 3. Option A (10%) is not a standard sub-target. 4. Option B (12%) is Weaker Sections. 5. Option D (7.5%) is Micro Enterprises. 6. Therefore, Agriculture is 18%.

questions.text: The ratio of the speeds of two trains is 3:4. The slower train takes 2 hours more than the faster train to cover a distance of 480 km. What is the speed of the faster train (in km/h)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Let speeds be 3x and 4x. Time difference = 480/(3x) - 480/(4x) = 2 → 480*(1/12x)=2 → 40/x=2 → x=20 → faster speed = 4x = 80 km/h. Full steps: Distance = 480 km. Time taken by slower = 480/(3x), by faster = 480/(4x). Their difference is 2 hours. Solving gives x=20, so faster train speed = 4*20 = 80 km/h.

questions.text: As per the amendment to the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) Act, 1961, which came into effect from September 1, 2021, what is the maximum insurance cover payable to a depositor per insured bank?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate ₹1 Lakh (pre-2020 limit) and ₹10 Lakh (never implemented); the 2021 Budget announcement hiked cover to ₹5 Lakh. Step-by-step: The DICGC Act was amended in August 2021, raising the deposit insurance limit from ₹1 Lakh to ₹5 Lakh per depositor per bank, effective September 1, 2021, covering all commercial and cooperative banks.

questions.text: As per the RBI Master Direction on Priority Sector Lending (PSL) targets for Domestic Scheduled Commercial Banks, what is the specific sub-target prescribed for lending to 'Weaker Sections' as a percentage of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE), whichever is higher?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total PSL target is 40%; Agriculture is 18%. Weaker Sections is a distinct sub-target fixed at 12% (not 10% old, not 15/18% Agri/Total). Step-by-step: Under current PSL guidelines, Domestic Scheduled Commercial Banks must allocate 40% of ANBC/CEOBE to Priority Sector. Within this, a sub-target of 18% is for Agriculture and 12% is specifically earmarked for Weaker Sections (small/marginal farmers, artisans, SC/ST, etc.).

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error-free, select 'No Error'. The proposed amendment seeks to not only enhance (A) / the capital buffers but also improving (B) / the governance standards of (C) / urban cooperative banks. (D)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Spot the correlative conjunction pair 'not only... but also'. The grammatical structures immediately following each connector must be parallel (same part of speech). Here, 'not only' is followed by the bare infinitive 'enhance' (governed by 'to' in 'seeks to'). Therefore, 'but also' must be followed by a bare infinitive ('improve'), not the gerund 'improving'. Step-by-step: 1. Locate the correlative conjunction pair: 'not only' (end of Part A) and 'but also' (start of Part B). 2. Identify the structure after 'not only': 'enhance' (bare infinitive, linked to the preceding 'to'). 3. Check the structure after 'but also': 'improving' (gerund/present participle). 4. Detect mismatch: Infinitive vs. Gerund violates parallelism. 5. Error lies in Part B. Correction: 'but also improve'.
